text:
GitHub Copilot in Teams: a notification can become a pull request.

The Oct. 23 update connects bug notifications to investigation, fixes, and a PR. People still review, test, and merge.

On Tech Thursday, we used Copilot CLI with MCP to generate images, then rejected results that missed the brief. Different surface. Same lesson: delegate the work, keep the judgment.

Try one reproducible bug in a test repo this week. The shift is from answering a message to handing off work.

Follow Layer8Culture if you're building with AI.

text:
GitHub Copilot in Teams just shortened the path from bug report to pull request.

What changed: GitHub's Oct. 23 update brings notifications and Copilot into the consolidated GitHub app for Teams.

What it does: a bug notification can lead to an @GitHub mention that investigates, proposes a fix, and opens a PR. Your team still reviews, tests, and merges.

Why builders should care: the useful unit isn't another answer in chat. It's a change someone can inspect.

We saw the creative version on Tech Thursday: Copilot CLI used MCP to generate a batch of images. The first results missed the quality bar. Connecting the tool didn't remove the need for judgment. That was a CLI experiment, not a Teams demo.

Try this week:
1. Update or install the consolidated GitHub app in Teams. Connect your account and choose a test repository when prompted.
2. Use a small, reproducible bug with expected behavior and a clear pass/fail check.
3. Ask @GitHub to investigate and propose a fix. Inspect the diff and run the check before anyone merges.

If you use the legacy app, GitHub says it retires Nov. 16.

The signal: AI is moving from prompts into handoffs. Keep a human at the decision point.

Save this for your next workflow test.

AI video transitions need a shared frame, not just a similar mood.

The practical detail from our latest Tech Thursday: six stills became the anchors for five clips.

Clip one: frame 1 to frame 2.
Clip two: frame 2 to frame 3.

Frame 2 does two jobs: ending one shot and starting the next. That common anchor helps continuity; you still have to inspect the join.

Before spending on the full sequence, render two neighboring clips. Check subject, lighting, position, and motion at the cut. A beautiful shot can still be the wrong neighbor.
